newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand seeks IMF, Australia help after float.
newsitem.headline: Thailand seeks IMF, Australia help after float.

text.p: Thailand has sought technical assistance from the International Monetary Fund and the Reserve Bank of Australia after floating its baht currency, Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Wednesday.
"We have notified the IMF this morning and have asked for technical assistance from the IMF and the Reserve Bank of Australia," he told a news conference.
Rerngchai said he sought advice from the Australian central bank because the country had long experience in handling managed floats over the past 10 years.
"The central bank notified the IMF about the (float) decision at dawn today. We also informed our neighbours in the region as they could also be affected," he told the news conference.

"As for IMF, we need the technical assistance to improve the implementation of our monetary policy, the supervision of financial institutions -- to make it accomodative to the new system which is more liberalised," Rerngchai said.

Thailand said early on Wednesday that it would adopt a managed float of its baht and discontinue the fixing of the currency on a daily basis pegged to a trade-weighted basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar.
